lots.what_it_is: Two oval gold-coloured cufflinks with torpedo-style swivel backs (one face engraved with a script monogram, the other plain). One link is stamped 14K with an 81R number; the second link's stamp is not legible in the photos. Gowans title: 14K gold cufflink and 1 other cufflink, 4.4g total.

sold.note: SOLD, AUD, same_item: category guide only. Page opened (archive search results): 9ct gold cufflinks, 2.62g, engraved thin rectangles, dumbbell fittings, attributed to Willis & Sons, estimate $150, SOLD $140. Matched 9ct pair, not 14K, not oval, not a mismatched pair. Noble does not say whether the realised price includes premium. Not used for any maximum bid.

lots.guide_summary: No same-item or close entries survive. The researcher returned no entries (search budget exhausted, and it was still exhausted for this check). The only priced reference is one category-guide SOLD result (a light 9ct pair, 2.62g, A$140 hammer or realised, Noble, Nov 2025), which is a different carat and a matched pair. Value here rests mostly on gold content: if the 14K link is about half of the 4.4g, that is roughly 2.2g of 14K (about 1.3g fine gold); the other link may be lower carat or gold-filled. Spot gold was not checked. All prices AUD, no conversion.
lots.working: No same-item SOLD evidence, so keep_max_hammer = 0 and flip_max_hammer = 0. The single Noble result is a category guide (9ct matched pair) and cannot set a maximum. Buyer's premium for reference: all-in = hammer x 1.198.
lots.confidence_reason: Only one link's mark (14K) is read; the second mark is illegible; no same-item sold evidence; scrap value not calculated because spot gold was not checked.
lots.dropped_entries: None to drop: the researcher supplied no entries.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 1: two oval links, about the same size and form, left engraved with an ornate script monogram, right plain and scratched; both have oval bean-shaped toggle backs on a short post. Photo 2 (enlarged): the reverse of one face is clearly stamped '14K' with '81R' above it (likely a pattern or maker's number, typical of American-made links). Photo 3 (cropped, enlarged and rotated): the second link's back carries a stamp beginning with '1' followed by worn characters (possibly '10K', '1/20 12K' or a gold-filled mark); I could not read it reliably. This agrees with the Gowans title that only one link is 14K.
lots.condition: Surface scratches on both faces, monogram engraving worn but clear, no obvious dents or broken toggles visible. Mismatched pair (one engraved, one plain), which limits resale as jewellery.
lots.question_for_gowans: What is the mark on the second (plain or engraved?) cufflink: 10K, 14K, gold-filled or rolled gold? What does each link weigh separately, and do the toggles swivel and hold?

lots.what_it_is: Free-form pale blue opal (flat, probably a doublet or a thin solid on dark backing, not confirmed) in a small yellow-metal claw cap and bail, on a fine yellow snake chain with lobster clasp. Gowans title: opal pendant on 9ct gold chain. No stamps visible in the single photo.

sold.note: SOLD, AUD, same_item: close. Page opened: 'Opal pendant, oval cabochon opal set in a 9ct yellow gold floral pendant, hallmarked 9ct. Toned, very fine', estimate $200, sold $160. Oval cabochon not free-form, no chain, opal quality not described. Premium inclusion not stated.

SOLD, AUD, same_item: close. Page opened: 'Opal pendant, set in 9ct gold surround mount, with gold plated chain (pendant total weight 10.05g; 16.86g with chain)', estimate $150, sold $190. Much heavier gold mount than ours, plated (not gold) chain. Premium inclusion not stated.

SOLD, AUD, same_item: category guide. Page opened: 9ct opal doublet pendant, 3.35g, 17x24mm, by Wendt (a collected Australian maker), estimate $200, sold $280. Maker premium makes it a high outlier; not used in the guide range.

lots.guide_summary: Two close SOLD results (9ct-mounted opal pendants, Noble Sydney, Nov 2025, A$160 and A$190) and one category-guide SOLD (Wendt-made doublet pendant, A$280, excluded from the range). No unsold or asking evidence. All AUD, no conversion. Noble does not state whether realised prices include premium. Opal pendant values depend almost entirely on opal type and colour, which cannot be judged from one photo, so these are a guide, not a basis for a bid.
lots.working: The surviving SOLD entries are close, not the same item: opal type (solid, doublet or triplet), brightness and the gold weight of the chain all differ and are unconfirmed here, so no maximum bid is set. For reference only, if the opal and chain prove comparable at the viewing, the lowest close sale A$160 / 1.198 = A$133.56, rounded down = A$130 hammer would be the keep ceiling. The lot already has 5 bids.
lots.confidence_reason: One photo only; no 9ct stamp read on chain or mount; opal type unconfirmed; comparables are close rather than same-item.
lots.dropped_entries: Researcher supplied no entries. I did not use Noble Sale 136 lot 279 (small white opal 9ct pendant, A$110, 29 Jul to 2 Aug 2024) because it is just over 24 months old and much smaller, or Sale 136 lot 282 (five chains with a small doublet, A$40), which is a mixed lot.
lots.key_photo_findings: Enlarged crop: the opal is a flat, elongated free-form, pale milky blue with weak visible play of colour in this photo; a dark edge on the left side suggests a dark backing (doublet) or potch, not confirmed. Held only at the top by a scalloped claw cap with a tube bail. Chain is a fine round snake chain with lobster clasp and end caps; colour consistent with yellow gold but no stamp legible.
lots.condition: Looks clean and intact in the photo; no chips visible at this resolution. Opal edges and backing not seen.
lots.question_for_gowans: Is the 9ct stamp on the chain, the pendant mount, or both? What do the chain and pendant weigh? Is the opal a doublet, triplet or solid (check the side for a dark backing line), and is it chipped or crazed?

Gowans title: sterling silver vesta, Birmingham, on chain with 3 coins. Hallmarks not visible in the photo.

lots.guide_summary: Four SOLD results from Noble Numismatics, Sydney (Nov 2025 and Apr 2026): three single sterling vestas at A$50, A$50 and A$70, and a vesta-plus-coin-items bundle at A$130. No unsold or asking evidence. All AUD, no conversion. Noble does not state whether realised prices include premium. None includes a silver albert chain, which would add value if the chain is silver (not confirmed).
lots.working: keep: lowest close SOLD = A$50 (Noble lots 3254 and 3255, Nov 2025, single sterling vestas). The Gowans lot is a vesta plus chain and coins, so a vesta-only price is a conservative floor. 50 / 1.198 = 41.74, rounded down = A$40 hammer (A$47.92 all-in). flip: likely resale about A$90 for the vesta, chain and coins together (between the A$70 single vesta and the A$130 bundle). Less about 13% selling fees (A$11.70) and A$12 outbound postage = A$66.30; / 2.396 = 27.67, rounded down = A$25 hammer. Flipping is not worthwhile at that margin.
lots.confidence_reason: Hallmarks not read (Birmingham and sterling claims unverified); chain metal unknown; only 2 of the 3 coins visible; SOLD support is close (vesta alone) rather than the same item, though 4 pages were opened.
lots.dropped_entries: Researcher supplied no entries. Older Noble results seen but not used because they are well over 24 months old: Sale 96 lot 2819 (Birmingham 1888 George Unite vesta with sterling fob chain, A$80), Sale 91 lot 1260 (vesta with two fob chains, A$40), Sale 77 lot 970 (vesta, silver fob chain with jetons and coin and a 9ct fob, A$50), Sale 46 lot 1294 (silver vesta with fob chain, A$120). They suggest the same modest level for this type.
lots.key_photo_findings: Single photo. Vesta: rectangular with rounded corners, hinged lid, side striker area, engraved foliate scroll with a vacant shield cartouche, worn; no hallmark visible on the face shown. Chain: fancy pierced barrel or bookchain-style links with a T-bar or clasp at one end, colour matching the vesta. Coins (enlarged): the larger reads '...LLING' with a laurel wreath, consistent with a Victorian 'ONE SHILLING' reverse; the smaller shows a crowned shield or monogram design, possibly a threepence or sixpence. The third coin in the title is not visible.
lots.condition: Vesta worn with light scratches; engraving softened; dents not visible from this angle. Coins worn and soldered or looped to the chain (holed or mounted coins have no numismatic premium).
lots.question_for_gowans: Can you confirm the vesta hallmark (Birmingham anchor, lion and date letter) and whether the chain is also hallmarked silver? What is the total weight? Where is the third coin, and are the coins silver?
